definitions.explanation: A visible indication or symbol that represents something.
Something that serves as evidence or a sign of something else.

examples.japanese: {地図|ちず}に{印|しるし}をつけた。
examples.english: I put a mark on the map.

examples.japanese: {大事|だいじ}な{所|ところ}に{印|しるし}をつけておく。
{赤|あか}い{印|しるし}がある{箇所|かしょ}を{確認|かくにん}してください。
examples.english: Please check the places with red marks.

examples.japanese: これは{感謝|かんしゃ}の{印|しるし}です。
examples.english: This is a token of my gratitude.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{成功|せいこう}は{努力|どりょく}の{印|しるし}だ。
examples.english: His success is proof of his effort.

examples.japanese: {友情|ゆうじょう}の{印|しるし}として{指輪|ゆびわ}を{交換|こうかん}した。
examples.english: We exchanged rings as a token of our friendship.

notes:
{印|しるし} can refer to both physical marks and abstract symbols or tokens.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {印|しるし}をつける (to put a mark)
- {感謝|かんしゃ}の{印|しるし} (token of gratitude)
- {愛|あい}の{印|しるし} (sign of love)
- {成功|せいこう}の{印|しるし} (sign of success)

RELATED READINGS:
The kanji {印|しるし} has multiple readings:
- しるし (native Japanese reading)
- いん (Sino-Japanese reading, used in compounds like {印象|いんしょう})
